reasons: Failures are handled: write errors are logged, a lost browser is restarted and a failed launch is retried after a pause.
No test in the packet covers the queue, the resume step or the card logic.
The queue state is held in memory, so behaviour across several server processes is not covered.

terms.meaning: one execution of a review tool, with its own sequence of events
a web browser run in the background without a window, used to take screenshots
a library that controls a web browser from code
a screenshot of a source page with the quoted passage outlined
a waiting line that processes items in order, a few at a time
how many items are processed at the same time

used_by: the run stage code of the review tools (not listed in the packet)

sections.name: File setup, RunTool
sections.title: Feed setup and run tools
sections.what: States what the feed records and the order its events come in, and names the three review tools that use it.
sections.why: Likely reason: the order is what lets a viewer rebuild each card, so it is described at the top.
sections.watch_out: Changing the event order breaks the way the viewer groups cards.

sections.name: RunEventType
sections.title: Kinds of event
sections.what: Lists the kinds of event a run can record, from source opened through screenshot, capture result, value, check and decision, to metric and stage notes.
sections.why: Likely reason: the viewer shows each kind differently, so the list must stay complete.
sections.watch_out: A new kind must also be handled by the viewer or it may not show.

sections.name: EmitInput, Row
sections.title: Input and stored row shapes
sections.what: Describes what a stage passes in to record an event, and the stored row that results.
sections.why: Likely reason: all stages share one way of writing events.
sections.watch_out: Messages are cut to 2,000 characters, so long text is silently shortened.

sections.name: RunEventLog, logs
sections.title: Run event log
sections.what: Holds the next sequence number and a short buffer for one run, writes events to the database in batches of up to 200, and clears a stage's old events when it runs again.
sections.why: Likely reason: batching reduces database writes, and clearing old events stops a re-run from showing duplicate cards.
sections.watch_out: Events in the buffer are lost if the process stops before a flush. Writes that fail are only logged.

sections.name: runEventLog
sections.title: Getting a run's event log
sections.what: Returns the one event log for a run in this process, creating it from the highest saved sequence number on first use. Keeps at most 200 logs in memory.
sections.why: Likely reason: the stage code and the capture queue must share one sequence so the order stays right.
sections.watch_out: Two processes would each create a log and could write duplicate sequence numbers.

sections.name: CardSource
sections.title: Source details for a card
sections.what: Describes the source behind a card: its web address, quote, publisher, title and date.
sections.why: Likely reason: a card shows the source and its exact quote as evidence.
sections.watch_out: Missing fields are allowed, so a card can be shown with little source detail.

sections.name: sourceIdFor, CaptureRow
sections.title: Finding or creating a source
sections.what: Returns the id of the source for a web address and quote, creating it if it does not exist. Returns nothing when there is no web address or quote.
sections.why: Likely reason: every card needs a stored source so its screenshot and vetting can attach.
sections.watch_out: A failed creation returns nothing, which silently removes the screenshot path for that card.

sections.name: captureCard
sections.title: Shape of a screenshot card
sections.what: Builds the details the viewer needs to show a stored screenshot: its id, image address, label, page, layer, environment, capture time and matched text.
sections.why: Likely reason: the viewer loads images by id, so the card carries the address.
sections.watch_out: The image address is a fixed path, so changing the route breaks old cards.

sections.name: failureCard
sections.title: Shape of a failure card
sections.what: Builds a readable failure reason from a stored capture result, such as the quote being found on the page but no image taken, or the status text.
sections.why: Likely reason: people need a plain reason for each failed capture.
sections.watch_out: The reason text is cut at the first part of the stored note, so any detail after that is not shown.

sections.name: latestGenuine
sections.title: Finding the newest good screenshot
sections.what: For a list of sources, returns the newest genuine stored screenshot for each one that has an image.
sections.why: Likely reason: a source with a good screenshot should reuse it instead of capturing again.
sections.watch_out: Only results marked genuine are used, so a genuine but unmarked image is ignored.

sections.name: freshServiceResult
sections.title: Recent capture service result
sections.what: Returns the latest capture result for this environment if it is still valid: a found result is always valid, a failure is valid for a set number of days.
sections.why: Likely reason: failed captures are not retried every time, to save time and load on websites.
sections.watch_out: The retry window is set by a constant, so changing it changes how often failed pages are tried again.

sections.name: emitScreenshotState, waiting
sections.title: Showing a screenshot state for a source
sections.what: After a card opens, shows what the screenshot is: a stored image, an alternative source's image, a recent failure, or a new capture queued. A source with no web address gets a message saying so.
sections.why: Likely reason: the viewer needs one clear screenshot state for each card as soon as it opens.
sections.watch_out: When a capture is queued, the card waits for the queue, so a stopped queue leaves cards stuck on queued.

sections.name: order, captureQueueState
sections.title: Queue settings and state
sections.what: Holds the process-wide waiting order, the number of running captures, the browser, and the time before which a failed browser launch is not retried. Concurrency comes from an environment variable and defaults to two.
sections.why: Likely reason: one browser per process is shared by all runs, so these must live at process level.
sections.watch_out: The concurrency setting is read once at start, so changing it needs a restart.

sections.name: queuedForRun
sections.title: Captures waiting for a run
sections.what: Counts how many captures are still waiting for one run.
sections.why: Likely reason: the viewer shows how many screenshots are still to come.
sections.watch_out: Counts sources that are waiting, not cards, so one source shared by several cards is counted once.

sections.name: resumed
sections.title: Resume flag
sections.what: Records which runs have already had their waiting captures resumed in this process.
sections.why: Likely reason: resuming should happen once per run after a restart, not on every read.
sections.watch_out: The flag lives in memory and resets on restart, which is when it is needed.

sections.name: resumeQueuedCaptures
sections.title: Resuming captures after a restart
sections.what: After a server restart, re-queues every capture a run was still waiting on, using the events saved in the database. Does nothing if the run already has captures waiting.
sections.why: Likely reason: the queue is in memory, so without this, queued screenshots would never finish.
sections.watch_out: Only the first feed read after restart triggers this, so runs nobody views are not resumed.

sections.name: queueCapture
sections.title: Adding a source to the queue
sections.what: Adds a source to the waiting list. If it is already waiting, the run is added to its list of waiting runs instead, so one capture serves all of them.
sections.why: Likely reason: the same source often appears in several runs, and one capture is enough.
sections.watch_out: The list of waiting runs is checked by identity, so two log objects for one run would both be served.

sections.name: getBrowser
sections.title: Getting the shared browser
sections.what: Returns the shared browser, starting it if needed. After a failed start it refuses for five minutes instead of retrying each time.
sections.why: Likely reason: starting a browser is slow and can fail, so it is started once and the failure is remembered.
sections.watch_out: Any caller during the five-minute pause gets an error, so a bad browser setup blocks every capture for that time.

sections.name: pump
sections.title: Starting queued work
sections.what: Starts waiting captures while fewer than the allowed number are running. When everything is done, it closes the shared browser after a minute with no work.
sections.why: Likely reason: it limits how many pages are open at once and frees resources when idle.
sections.watch_out: The idle close is scheduled from a timer, and new work cancels it, so a busy queue keeps the browser open.

sections.name: work
sections.title: Running one capture and reporting it
sections.what: Takes one source, captures it with its alternatives, and sends the result to every run waiting on it. Each card gets a screenshot, an alternative screenshot, or a failure reason. If the browser was lost, it restarts it once. Any other error becomes a service failure on every card.
sections.why: Likely reason: one capture is shared by many cards, so its result has to be reported to each of them.
sections.watch_out: The failure path reports the same error to every waiting card, so one broken source can mark many cards failed.

sections.name: cardsForSource
sections.title: Finding the cards for a source
sections.what: Lists the cards in a run that asked for a capture of one source and have not yet got a result.
sections.why: Likely reason: results must reach exactly the cards still waiting, and no others.
sections.watch_out: It matches on the card key stored in the event payload, so a payload without that key is not found.

sections.name: SourceCardInput
sections.title: Shape of the source card input
sections.what: Describes what a stage gives to open a card: the card key, stage, project, label, source, whether the value came from the Yard or was newly found, the value, unit, basis tags, translation and extra details.
sections.why: Likely reason: each stage opens cards the same way, so the viewer receives consistent data.
sections.watch_out: Translations are only shown when the language is not English, which hides English translations on purpose.

sections.name: openSourceCard, CheckTest
sections.title: Opening a value card
sections.what: Records that a source was opened, runs the screenshot state step, then records the value found, its quote, basis tags and any translation. Returns the source id.
sections.why: Likely reason: the card should show the source first, then its screenshot, then the value.
sections.watch_out: The source lookup can return nothing, in which case the screenshot states that there is no source to outline.

sections.name: emitChecks
sections.title: Recording checks
sections.what: Records a check result with a summary: how many checks failed and which, or that all passed.
sections.why: Likely reason: the reviewer should see which checks failed without opening each one.
sections.watch_out: Checks marked as not run are not counted as failures, so a blank result can look like a pass.

sections.name: emitDecision
sections.title: Recording a decision
sections.what: Records whether a value was accepted, not used or held, with a note explaining why.
sections.why: Likely reason: the reason behind each decision must be kept with the run.
sections.watch_out: The outcome is only three fixed words, so any other outcome is not accepted by the type.

summary: Writes the live feed shown while a review run works: each step records what it opened, what screenshot it got, what value it found and what check it made, and screenshots are captured through a shared queue.
purpose: Lets a reviewer watch a run as it happens and see the evidence behind each value, with a screenshot where one can be taken.
why: Likely reason: a run can take a long time, and each value needs visible evidence, so events are streamed as they happen.
how: Each run has one event log with an increasing sequence number. Events are buffered and written in batches. When a source is opened, the code looks for a stored screenshot, a screenshot from an alternative source or a recent failure, and otherwise queues a capture. A single process-wide queue runs up to a set number of captures at once in one shared browser, closes the browser after an idle minute, and reports results back to every run that asked for that source. After a restart, queued captures for a run are queued again once.
inputs: Run identifiers, stage names, source web addresses and quotes, values and checks from the calling stage, and the screenshot environment settings.
outputs: Rows in the run_event table, and screenshot and failure cards that the feed displays.
risks: The queue and the waiting list live only in memory, so they are lost on restart and only resumed for runs that are read again. A browser that fails to start blocks captures for five minutes. Concurrency is set by an environment variable.
debug: If cards stay queued, check captureQueueState and whether the browser can start. If events are missing, check the console for run_event write failures, since failures are logged and do not stop the run. If a stage shows duplicate cards, check resetStage and the card keys.
